answer: Thirty cipher locks open at each epoch's nadir. One claimant decodes one lock in a twenty-minute window; its key turns each block, so nothing pre-solves; three strangers sign, two each. Entry locks 85 POA, +50 per extra fake from one root: ten fakes lock 3,100 POA. One operator decodes two max: ten fakes need five hands, ten decodes, thirty signatures, fifteen strangers. Each extra fake from one root adds eight bits; the tenth runs 72 bits deeper, past the window. A missed nadir burns 30; one hand on two locks voids both. The ledger files each decode's delta and matches times to roots.
